hero.title: ITM University, Gwalior
hero.summary: ITM University’s School of Agriculture in Gwalior offers a broad bachelor’s degree and an agronomy master’s route. Its published teaching resources include an instructional farm and subject laboratories. Student READY work and agriculture research partnerships connect crop science with practical training and the needs of farming communities.

overview.heading: From agricultural foundations to agronomy specialisation
paragraphs: ITM’s agriculture bachelor’s curriculum is organised around fundamental sciences, production systems and later skill development. The university’s brochure places the school at its Sithouli setting and identifies an instructional farm, laboratory and library resources. A separate agronomy master’s course provides a focused postgraduate route.

The programme pages identify agriculture partnerships with research institutions and describe Student READY learning. For career comparisons, ITM also publishes an agriculture-and-allied-sector NIRF submission with dated undergraduate and postgraduate outcomes. These grouped returns are more specific than the university’s overall salary counters, though they still should not be read as a guarantee for one degree or a future student.

admissions.intro: The central eligibility page and individual course pages provide useful entry information. The agronomy pages use differing marks/qualification wording, so applicants should obtain the applying-year rule in writing.

scholarships.text: ITM’s 2026 policy describes merit, sports and special-category support, with continuation conditions involving attendance, backlogs and conduct. A specific agriculture award requires confirmation.

placements.text: The NIRF 2026 agriculture-and-allied return reports 97 placed graduates from 114 four-year undergraduate completers in 2024–25, with 14 selected for higher study. The reported median salary applies to placed graduates in that grouped return.

faqs.question: Which ITM institution is this?
faqs.answer: This is ITM University in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, with its official address on NH-44, Jhansi Road.

faqs.question: How long are the two listed courses?
faqs.answer: The bachelor’s degree is four years; the agronomy master’s is described as two years.

faqs.question: What practical resource is described in the brochure?
faqs.answer: The agriculture school’s brochure identifies an instructional farm.

faqs.question: Why should agronomy applicants confirm eligibility?
faqs.answer: The course page, FAQ and central table use different qualifying-degree and marks wording.

faqs.question: Are the placement figures from the whole university?
faqs.answer: The figures here are from the agriculture-and-allied NIRF return, grouped by programme length; they are not a B.Sc.-only outcome.

faqs.question: What is the ICAR term for the listed programmes?
faqs.answer: The audited record runs from 29 July 2024 to 28 July 2029 and includes B.Sc. Agriculture and M.Sc. Agronomy.
